brief.conference_theme: Environmental and social regeneration: beyond sustainability
brief.panel_theme: Circularity at scale: regenerative sourcing and supply chains

plan.summary: Find a three-person panel on circularity at scale, regenerative sourcing, and supply chains for a business audience. Favor rising and established speakers suited to a small budget, with prior conference or presentation experience; diversify sectors, career stages, places, and organization types, with national reach and no New Haven-only constraint.

angles: Researchers on circular supply chains and regenerative sourcing at Yale School of the Environment and Yale School of Management; identify faculty who present at Academy of Management or Sustainable Supply Chain conferences

Business-school scholars studying industrial ecology, circular economy, or supply-chain sustainability at universities such as MIT Sloan and University of Michigan Ross; prioritize conference presenters

Corporate circularity and responsible-sourcing directors at companies featured in Ellen MacArthur Foundation case studies or the World Business Council for Sustainable Development; look for speakers at Circularity or GreenBiz events

Supply-chain sustainability and regenerative agriculture practitioners at B Corps, major food and apparel companies, or certification organizations such as Textile Exchange; prioritize public conference presenters

Circular-economy and sustainable procurement officials at US EPA, state environmental agencies, and the US Department of Agriculture; seek presenters at National Recycling Coalition or sustainable procurement conferences
Trade and supply-chain policy experts at Resources for the Future, World Resources Institute, or the OECD working on circular materials and regenerative sourcing; prioritize public event speakers
Founders of circular materials, reuse, and supply-chain traceability businesses appearing in Circularity conference programs or Ellen MacArthur Foundation network profiles
Regenerative agriculture and sustainable-sourcing startup founders in Food System 6, New York Climate Week, or Climate Collective event programs; favor emerging speakers
Sourcing and labor-rights advocates at As You Sow, Oxfam America, and the Responsible Business Alliance addressing supply-chain accountability; look for conference presenters

Regenerative agriculture and circular-economy nonprofit leaders at Regenerative Organic Alliance, National Farm to School Network, or US Green Building Council events; prioritize practitioners with speaking experience
Business and supply-chain reporters covering circularity and sourcing at GreenBiz, Trellis, and Bloomberg; identify journalists who moderate or speak at Circularity events
Sustainability editors and authors at Supply Chain Dive, Just Food, and Textile Exchange conference programs covering regenerative sourcing and circular supply chains

cards.name: Yuan Yao
cards.job_title: Manufacturer’s Association Professor of Industrial Ecology and Sustainable Systems; Director, Center for Industrial Ecology
cards.organization: Yale School of the Environment, Yale University
cards.could_speak_on: How circular-economy strategies, biomass-based materials, and systems analysis can help businesses scale regenerative sourcing and production.

Life-cycle assessment for circular sourcing decisions
Modeling the environmental and societal effects of sustainable production
cards.bio: Yuan Yao is the Manufacturer’s Association Professor of Industrial Ecology and Sustainable Systems at Yale School of the Environment and directs Yale’s Center for Industrial Ecology. Her research develops systems-analysis methods for industrial systems, with current projects focused on the bioeconomy and sustainable production.
credentials: PhD in Chemical Engineering, Northwestern University
U.S. National Science Foundation CAREER Award

cards.why_fit: A strong match for a business-facing panel on circularity at scale: she connects industrial systems research and modeling with sustainable production and biomass-based materials, and has presented on circular economy in the forest sector.

past_speaking.event: Yale Forest Forum: “Planted Forests and Circular Economy”
Yale Alumni Academy: “Bioeconomy, Forests, and Climate Change”

notable_work: Research projects on the bioeconomy and sustainable production

Looking for people who would make great panels together…
Suggested 3 panel(s): From Feedstock to Factory: Scaling Regenerative Materials; Circularity in the Real Economy; Making Sourcing Accountable

panels.title: From Feedstock to Factory: Scaling Regenerative Materials
panels.question: How can businesses scale circular supply chains that source regenerative materials while delivering credible environmental and business value?

members.name: Alysia Garmulewicz
members.angle: She brings a startup perspective on using open data, AI, and regional biomaterials research to develop scalable regenerative feedstocks.

members.name: Yuan Yao
members.angle: She brings systems analysis and life-cycle assessment to evaluate circular-economy pathways and bio-based materials.

members.name: Ben Christensen
members.angle: He brings experience connecting traceable domestic wood supply chains and regenerative feedstocks with large-scale buyers.

moderator.name: Heather Clancy
moderator.angle: She can guide a business-focused discussion of how innovation and technology are changing corporate approaches to regenerative supply chains.

why_together: The panel spans materials innovation, systems-level evaluation, and the path from feedstock suppliers to industrial buyers.
Their different vantage points make it possible to examine both the promise of regenerative materials and the practical work of scaling procurement.
panels.tension: The founders focus on getting new feedstocks and supply-chain models to market; Yao’s systems perspective can probe whether scale delivers robust environmental benefits.
panels.balance_note: A mix of startup and academic perspectives, with a national business audience in mind; all are established or rising voices, and the panelists have prior speaking experience.

panels.title: Circularity in the Real Economy
panels.question: What does it take to turn circularity from a corporate ambition into a durable supply-chain system?

members.name: Allison Lin
members.angle: She brings a global food-company perspective on coordinating circularity, packaging, and ecosystem goals across business segments and partners.

members.name: Amy Lee
members.angle: She brings a manufacturing perspective on circular product design and building partner and customer models to return materials to productive use.

members.name: Marian Chertow
members.angle: She brings research on industrial symbiosis as a way to organize material, energy, and by-product exchanges across companies and communities.

moderator.name: Richard Martin
moderator.angle: He can moderate through the lens of circular product development and the business transition away from linear models.

why_together: They connect corporate strategy and product design with the broader networks needed to circulate materials.
Their examples span food and manufacturing, while Chertow’s industrial-symbiosis lens widens the discussion beyond a single company.
panels.tension: Corporate programs and product-level recovery may move at a different pace from the cross-company coordination and community infrastructure required for industrial symbiosis.
panels.balance_note: Two corporate practitioners and a Yale academic offer complementary organizational and systems perspectives; all have prior speaking experience.

panels.title: Making Sourcing Accountable
panels.question: How can businesses scale circular and regenerative sourcing while accounting for both material impacts and people across the supply chain?

members.name: Sreedevi Rajagopalan
members.angle: She brings research on data-driven sustainable sourcing, Scope 3 emissions, supplier engagement, and the role of smaller firms.

members.name: James Gyenes
members.angle: He brings a responsible-business perspective on supply-chain due diligence, labor rights, and worker protections in global value chains.

members.name: Kelly McBee
members.angle: She brings investor-advocacy experience pressing companies to reduce virgin-material use and make packaging commitments measurable.

moderator.name: Agnieszka de Sousa
moderator.angle: She can connect supply-chain choices to global food markets, sourcing pressures, and resilience.

why_together: The discussion links environmental measurement and supplier engagement with labor accountability and corporate oversight.
The panel can test whether circular sourcing commitments translate into measurable, responsible changes across value chains.
panels.tension: Measurement and corporate targets can create momentum, while advocates may press on whether commitments deliver accountability for workers and reductions in virgin-material extraction.
panels.balance_note: The panel combines academic, advocacy, and business-accountability perspectives with experience relevant to national supply chains; all panelists have prior speaking or presenting experience.
